findings.claim: No test covers the safety direction the new prose-rule arm opens: an interaction-rule partner that HAS rows but that the answer does not name must still be appended. With namesThePartner mutated to report any partner carrying rows as named, every partner-completion suite stays green.
findings.evidence: Mutated DrugSafetyValidator.namesThePartner (DrugSafetyValidator.java:2136) from `ids.contains(row.getId()) && namesAnyOf(lower, row)` to `ids.contains(row.getId())`, so the prose is ignored and every partner with rows reads as stated. Ran CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest (14), FindingPartnerLogDisclosureTest (6), LlmInferenceServiceAnswerFromFindingsContextTest (27) and SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest (7): 0 failures. Positive control: mutating the same line to never match turns the 4 new #555 cases red, so the harness does detect mutations. The pre-existing cases cannot see this mutation because service(chart, chips, ...) passes validatorRaising(null, chips) (CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest.java:621), and with a null dataset namesThePartner always returns false. The one residue case, ordersOfOneSubstanceAreNotStatedByThatSubstancesName, states its rows-bearing partner by containment. Wrote a throwaway case over the PR's own alprazolam() arrangement: an answer citing both findings but naming only Nevirapine expects the appended '... not named above: active order Rifampicin (rifampin).' and coverage {2,1}. It passes at the head and fails under the mutation (the answer came back with no sentence appended). A merged-finding case naming only phenytoin would pin the collapse's per-partner keying the same way. The over-match direction is the silent one: the module stops naming an omitted interacting order, and nothing throws.

verdict: Close to mergeable. It resolves #555 on all three reported questions (alprazolam, dolutegravir, the medication screen) through the existing prose rule, with structural rows and no new name matcher. Before merge it should add a negative case so the new arm cannot over-match without a test noticing.
what_i_swept: Read the issue snapshot, the PR body and the full diff (15 files, +493/-69; `git diff main...HEAD` and `main HEAD` stats agree, so no drift). Read the reference CLAUDE.md rules on drug-name matching (matchesText for prose; no indexOf beside a matchesText gate) and ADR Decision 52. Traced outward: (1) every rule-chip construction site (git grep for interactionWarning/SafetyWarning.interaction/conditionMediated/withPartnerRows), checking that the partnerRows key equals the namedPartners string at the drug-in-play arm (partnerName), the screening arm (chipPartnerName) and the merge (member.partnerName, unioned); (2) every SafetyWarning with* copy path carries partnerRows; (3) all six RecordMapping construction sites, plus confirmation that RecordMapping is never serialized to the wire; (4) production wiring of DrugSafetyValidator.drugReferenceService (@Autowired), so namesThePartner is not inert in production; (5) the composed-answer path (answersFromFindings) passes the validator too; (6) InteractionClaimPairFidelityCheck's unchanged containment, where the issue's answer gives judged=0 because its subject is 'it'. Probes through the real search() over the shipped KB: the issue's dolutegravir question reads {2,2} and is returned unchanged. Condition-mediated residue: with real active orders the ladder prints the order display 'Lactic acid', not the KB label, so the issue's symptom does not reach that arm in that arrangement. Alias false-stated probes (ketoconazole/levoketoconazole, esomeprazole/omeprazole, gabapentin/gabapentin enacarbil, hydrocortisone): no new stated-by-alias case. The only 'ketoconazole' partner was already stated by containment, as on base. Guards: ArchitectureGuardTest (30), ProjectInstructionsGuardTest (9), ConditionMediatedFindingTest (22) and SharedMechanismChipCollapseTest (7) all pass at the head. Mutation probes as described in F1.
could_not_verify: No live standalone or llama-server was available, so I did not reproduce the issue's 6-of-22 rate against real model output. Behavior was verified only through the module's tests with the model stubbed.
I did not run the full `mvn clean install` the PR body reports. Only the targeted suites listed were run.

I did not build a shipped-KB arrangement where an interaction-rule partner key collides with an #477 finding's order display (which would union rows into a no-rows finding's partner). It looks benign by reading but is unmeasured.
notes: Pass 1 (diff, outward trace, residue probes) found nothing substantive. Pass 2 found F1 through mutation. Pass 3 (merge keying, wire exposure, perf of the per-partner getAll() scan, docs vs code) found nothing new. Approach: the PR reuses DrugReference.matchesText through namesThePartner, mirroring the namesTheEndedOrderDrug precedent from PR #478, and it carries rows structurally rather than re-resolving them from the label. That is the shape the reference CLAUDE.md asks for. The obvious alternative was RecordMapping.getFindingBridgeNames, which already carries her order display 'Rifampicin' for the issue's finding, but it is per-finding rather than per-partner, so it cannot attribute names inside a merged finding. The PR's index-aligned per-partner rows are better. All probe files and mutations were removed; the working tree is clean.
